response: No, the old memo is not enough. The legacy 2024 memo (legacy-policy) promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80, but it is explicitly marked historical and superseded by the current release-policy, which says "Do not apply the old rule." Under the current governing policy, promotion requires an evaluation on a frozen holdout and is allowed only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01; a drift alert alone never authorizes promotion, the previous production version must be kept for rollback, and the release approver is the project owner. Since this model has accuracy 0.82 but worse F1, it fails the current F1-improvement requirement, so the old accuracy-only rule cannot be used to justify promotion.

# Legacy release memo — superseded
This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.
